speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; to better understand your dizziness, nausea, and imbalance, could you please describe when these symptoms started and if anything makes them better or worse? Additionally, have you experienced any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or difficulty with coordination?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis. Your history of constant, low-grade vertigo starting this morning without hearing loss, despite recent viral symptoms, is classic for this condition. Since your symptoms improve slightly with rest and medication, this further supports an inner ear inflammation rather than a central cause.
